legibility: All nine crops show every sign and every label complete. 1518: the Wellcome scan is the larger (3328 px page) but several red labels are smeared and the final sign is over-inked; the LoC copy (2700 px page) has crisper red labels and a cleaner final sign - use both together. 1533: McGill (5560 px page) is the sharpest, then LoC (3344 px) and Jung/e-rara (2550 px); the signs agree in all three. 1651: archive.org 'threebooksoccult' is the cleaner image; Wellcome has heavy show-through but carries a rights statement. 1561 (BPL) is clear; 1613 (Naples/Google) is dark and soft but legible.
problems: 1518 red labels at positions 3 and 5 can be misread at first sight (position 3 looks like an 'e', position 5 like a 'c'). Compared with the black c and e in the alchemist's alphabet on the same page, they are the rotunda c (top stroke turned down) and e (thin rising stroke), so the labels run a-b-c-d-e in order. Do not 'correct' them.

1518: the red was printed in a separate pass and is out of register: fragments of the row-2 and row-3 labels touch the feet of the signs above them (in the Wellcome copy, e.g. under the d, e, f and h signs of row 1 and the k, p and q signs of row 2). These red marks are labels, not parts of the signs; trace the black only.

1518 sign for i: a small separate n-shaped element stands to the left of the U-shaped body; sign for r: a detached small foot below and right of the n-and-stem body. Both appear identically in the Wellcome and LoC copies, so they belong to the printed forme, not to damage. The 1561 French ('nU') and 1613 Latin ('nV') cuts keep the left element of the i sign; Agrippa 1533 and 1651 drop it.
1518 Wellcome: the final (w) sign is heavily over-inked and its lower right is a blot; the LoC copy shows the strokes more clearly.
1518 page shows show-through of the recto text (the Normanni alphabet passage) behind the table in both copies.

1533 McGill copy: no K label (a dot instead), plus stray inked dots after V and before the Omega. LoC prints 'K', Jung prints lower-case 'k'. A short rule appears under the M label in the LoC copy only.

1651: the final label is a small omega-like mark, not a capital Omega; both copies also show a small curved mark printed under the V label. Wellcome copy: heavy show-through of p. 437 (including the mirrored heading 'CHAP. XXIX ... Of the Characters and Seals of Spirits') behind the table; the crop includes the catchword 'CHAP.'.
threebooksoccult (1651) and the BPL 1561 scan carry no rights statement; McGill (1533) has none in the archive.org record.

archive.org display index versus image-file index: in b33552137 (Wellcome 1518), b30335231 (Wellcome 1651) and polygraphieetvni00trit (BPL 1561) the BookReader page nK shows image file K+1 (a leading colour card); in the McGill and Google (bub_gb_) items nK = file K. The page_url and image_url above were checked one by one.

Crops are lossless PNG re-encodings of the delivered images (JP2 masters decoded for Wellcome 1518, LoC 1518, LoC 1533, Wellcome 1651, BPL 1561 and Naples 1613; JPEG derivatives for McGill, Jung and threebooksoccult). No contrast change, rotation or cleanup.
notes: 1518 heading as printed (both copies, foot of 2q5r): 'Sequitur aliud alphabetum Honorij cognomento Thebani, cuius ministerio suas in magicis fatuitates abscondit, sicut Petrus de Apono testatur in suo maiore libro quarto.' This matches the Latin quoted by Peterson and Wikipedia; it is now checked against the print.

Book number: the text on 2p6r (Wellcome _0495), at the start of the Normanni chapter, reads 'In hoc libro sexto, qui & ultimus est, quosdam characteres veteres ... ab inferis statui revocare'; the OCR places the close of Book V ('quintum quoque Polygraphiae librum terminamus. Anno d[omi]ni M.D.VIII') on _0492 (OCR only, not viewed). The Theban table is therefore in Book VI of the 1518 Latin. The 1561 French prints it under the running head 'LIVRE CINQVIESME', which explains the 'Book V' reports.

Immediately before the Theban heading, on 2q5r, Trithemius says of the preceding cipher alphabet: 'Quamuis in latino sermone k y & w non sit nobis opus, quia tamen k & w in germanico utimur, ad numerum quartum atque uicesimum deduximus alphabetum ...' - his alphabets are brought to 24 places, with w for German. This is the context of the 'w' label on the final Theban sign (an observation about the page, not a claim about Trithemius's intent for the Theban table).

1533 wording (read in the McGill, LoC and Jung images, p. CCLXXIII): 'Ex horum itaque characterum genere sunt, quos notat Petrus Apponus ab Honorio Thebano traditos, quorum figura est talis ad nostrum alphabetum relata:'. The Latin form is 'Petrus Apponus'; 'fatuitates' does not occur. Chapter heading on p. CCLXXII: 'De characteribus & sigillis spirituum. Caput XXIX'.

1533 re-cuts the signs as smooth, even-stroked woodcut-like forms in 2 rows of 12 with roman capitals below; 1518 builds them from heavy blackletter-like pieces in 3 rows of 8 with red lower-case labels above. Visible structural differences (visual comparison, not measured): I (1518 has the extra left element), R (1518 n-and-stem with a detached foot; 1533/1651 an m-topped sign with a long right descender), V (1518 a V/Y with a small w-like stroke in its crook; 1533/1651 a bent, hooked angle without it), final sign (1518 no omega; 1533/1651 an omega at its foot). 1651 copies 1533 closely; its E has a closed curl at the top left where 1533 has an open hook.
The 1533 table's signs agree across LoC, McGill and Jung (same cuts); only the labels differ (K / none / k).

1613 Zetzner edition: the table is on p. 597 (sig. Pp3), with labels a-z and a final 'w', 3 rows of 8 like 1518. This confirms that Wikipedia's 'p. 597' belongs to the 1613 edition. Peterson's 'p. 579' was not matched (the 1600 Zetzner scan on archive.org, bub_gb_-D4XuQjTVhYC, has only 32 images and was not checked).
1561 French: labels a-z with 'u' in place of 'v' and '&' for the final sign; the heading names Honorius 'surnommé Thebanus' and does not name Pietro d'Abano.

A second 1518 copy was looked for on archive.org, e-rara (not found in a quick, non-exhaustive search) and MDZ (its search page needs JavaScript and was not usable); Gallica returned a Cloudflare block. The LoC copy was reached through its handle.

LoC 1533 sequence: image 0276 is p. CCLXVIII and 0277 is p. CCLXXIII, so pp. 269-272 are not at that point in the LoC image sequence (not investigated); the chapter opening was checked in the McGill and Jung copies.
Places of the 1518 Latin edition disagree: LoC '[Basel]' (from VD16), Wellcome '[Basle]'; the Boston Public Library record of the 1561 French says the Latin original 'appeared in Oppenheim, 1518'.

checked.method: Every crop and page view in this folder was viewed. Each crop was re-cut from a freshly downloaded master at the stated geometry and compared pixel by pixel (RMSE 0 for the JP2 and JPEG sources; 0.007 for the 1518 Wellcome IIIF JPEG, whose JP2 master then matched at 0). BookReader display indices were checked against each item's scandata.xml; loc.gov sequence numbers against the item JSON; the e-rara canvas against its IIIF manifest. Rights fields were re-read from archive.org metadata, loc.gov JSON and the e-rara manifest. Crop borders were tested for ink: no sign or label is cut in any crop.
confirmed: All nine crops show the named table complete, inside the stated running head / heading: 1518 2q5v under the q5r heading 'Sequitur aliud alphabetum Honorij cognomento Thebani'; 1533 'LIBER TERTIVS' p. CCLXXIII (LoC and McGill misnumbered 'CCXLXXIII', Jung 'CCLXXIII'), sig. 'z iii', chapter 'De characteribus & sigillis spirituum. Caput XXIX' on p. CCLXXII; 1651 '438 Of Occult Philosophy. Book III.'; 1561 'LIVRE CINQVIESME' fol. 184v ('DE POLYGRAPHIE. 184' on the recto); 1613 p. 597, 'Pp 3'.

Printed labels and their order are as listed for every plate (1518 a-h / i-q / r s t v x y z w; 1533 A-M and N-Z, Omega, with K / none / k in LoC / McGill / Jung; 1651 A-I / K-S / T V X Y Z small omega; 1561 a-h / i-q / r s t u x y z &; 1613 as 1518).
1518 labels 3 and 5 (which look like 'e' and 'c') are c and e: the black c and e of the alchemist's alphabet on the same page, in the same face, show the same two shapes in the same places.

Image indices: Wellcome 1518 n505 = leaf/file 0506 = IIIF $506 (leaf 0 is a non-access colour card); Wellcome 1651 n451 = leaf 0452; BPL 1561 n411 = leaf 0412; McGill n288 = leaf 288; Naples n666 = leaf 666; threebooksoccult n464 = leaf 464; LoC sp=502 = 0502.jp2, sp=277 = 0277.jp2; e-rara canvas 295 = image 1343489 labelled 'CCLXXIII'.

Rights statements for Wellcome 1518, Wellcome 1651, LoC 1518, LoC 1533, e-rara (Jung) and Naples (licenseurl only) quoted correctly; McGill, BPL 1561 and threebooksoccult have no rights or licence field.
corrected: 1518 (both plates): 'q4 and q5 unsigned' was wrong. q4r (_0503) is signed 'q iiij'; only q5 and q6 are unsigned. r1 is signed 'r' on _0509, so the table leaf is still 2q5v. Added the Book VI statement printed on q4r.

1533 LoC plate: the catalogue does not support '[Johannes Soter]' (LoC gives 's.n.') or a July 1533 date note (LoC's note reads 'MDXXIIII', a slip). The date now rests on the colophon itself, read in the Jung copy: 'Finis Anno M. D. XXXIII. Mense Iulio.' The same date reading was added to the McGill and Jung plates, with each printer attribution tied to its own record.
1533 LoC plate: 'DeOccultaPhilosophiaLoc1533' is an individual's archive.org upload, not an LoC mirror; its Public Domain Mark is the uploader's. Reworded the repository and rights fields.
